final_message:
Fixed. The bug was in `cancel` in `billing/subscriptions.py`. When called with `at_period_end=False`, it fell through to a stray `pass` and never moved the subscription to `canceled`. The failed payment then ran dunning's final action on a still-live subscription and set it to `unpaid`. I replaced the `pass` with `transition(ctx, subscription, "canceled")`.

I added your reproduction as `tests/test_dunning_cancel.py`. All 25 tests pass and mypy is clean. I also wrote `answer.json` as `{"file": "subscriptions.py", "function": "cancel"}`.

steps.command: sed -n 1,80p billing/dunning.py; sed -n 55,85p billing/engine.py; sed -n 38,60p billing/subscriptions.py
sed -n 155,215p billing/subscriptions.py; grep -n "def cancel" -A25 billing/engine.py; .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

python3 - <<'E'
p='billing/subscriptions.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('    pass\n    ctx.store.pending_items.pop','    transition(ctx, subscription, "canceled")\n    ctx.store.pending_items.pop',1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "subscriptions.py", "function": "cancel"}' > answer.json
cat >> tests/test_dunning_cancel.py <<'E'
def test_retries_exhausted_after_cancel_marks_uncollectible():
    from conftest import World

    w = World({"retry_offsets_days": [1], "final_action": "mark_unpaid"})
    cus = w.customer(last4="0002")
    sub = w.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(w.monthly["id"], 1)])
    w.engine.cancel(sub["id"], at_period_end=False)
    w.advance_days(1)
    [inv] = w.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert sub["status"] == "canceled"
    assert inv["status"] == "uncollectible"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -15; .venv/bin/python -m mypy billing | tail -3
